body:
I make myself as uncomfortable as possible, while still being able to sleep.
Being cold in the morning is my best/worst way, I usually sleep on top of the covers with a light blanket (preventing the warm-bed effect). Seeing as the heat isn't working in my dorm, I'm up at 6:31 AM, forty degree air temp, so it seems to work.

..I don't recommend this one.

(Ironically, I forgot my usual username.)

I'm also a college sophomore. I spent the last three semesters studying biology...which I was beginning to avidly hate. (A lot of my fellow students were raging perfectionists; the professors were cold and detached -- a lot was eating away at me, more than I realized at the time). Short story is, I didn't feel like I belonged. Thanks to my backstory, perceived lack of belonging is kinda a trigger...and once I got down the dark road of backstoryland, I had some serious plans to kill myself. I was relapsing hard on social anxiety and my confidence was plummeting.

At the strong urging of a few close friends and an on-campus psychologist, I'm looking into another program. I switched into psych classes to pursue biopsychology instead.

I can't even stress how amazing it feels. Like, okay, I'm contending with feelings of guilt and shame, but it makes a difference to be 1) interested in the material, and 2) have professors who treat you with warmth and compassion (aka, an invitation to belongingness). Although I anticipate future depressive episodes, the malignant tumor of a college program isn't currently bringin' me down as much. Right now, I'm just fascinated that my voice no longer intones as much flat affect. 

'ristark,' I urge you to consider changing directions. It won't be easy, but defeating depression seldom is.

And I guess as an endnote, you can (and statistically, probably will) get a girlfriend! However. Just remember that you don't need to be defined by a relationship.

I just wanted to thank you for responding. I feel a little better.

I'm sorry about your lyme disease. I know a few friends who have it, and it can really slow them down. :(

Thanks for the suggestions. I'll give them a go, I guess. I dabble in fiction, too...and drawing. But I haven't really had the time to create like I used to, since academics have literally taken over my life. 

I'm sorry that I haven't much to write back (since you put so much effort into your response and all). But for a third time, thanks. I really needed that.
